criteria.rationale: I examined the two sealed limits and their consumers. L1's dependence on an independent reviewer inspecting the displayed text is explicit and accepted for a single-spec review; L2 is supported by the limit's inclusion in the plan digest and optional bundle field. Semantic fit remains reviewer judgment, and N1 identifies the composite-scope ambiguity.
Composite review findings cannot unambiguously name one of two same-ID limits.
A limit with no text after the acceptance phrase passes validation.
The new limit identity contract is ambiguous when a plan contains multiple specs.
The ready-check accepts an unjustified limit; N1 also affects composite reviews.

D1 addresses non-convergence by recording an explicit reviewer classification; D2 binds the limits into the plan and bundle digests. The inspected implementation follows that design, with the specific defects reported separately. The structural assessment observed no deltas.
I compared the English and Portuguese manuals and their scaffold copies with runtime behavior: they describe the new section, sealed plan/bundle, review-brief/11 classification, and ready-check.
The ready-check reports unjustified limits in normal cases but gives a false pass when the reason phrase has no explanation.
R3 is ambiguous for composite scopes (N1); R4 also has false passes for empty reasons and partial ADR ID matches (N2, N3).
The inspected prepared subject contained the 18 implementation/documentation paths named by the spec artifacts, and the design assessment observed no structural delta.
A composite-scope finding can be accepted against an ambiguous same-ID limit, weakening the integrity of the approval classification.

The optional sealed field, versioned brief and typed finding field are a small sufficient design for preserving review-time assumptions; the digest omission preserves existing records. The reported defects are validation gaps, not speculative architecture.

findings.action: Composite roadmap or milestone plans append limits from multiple specs without preserving the source spec or checking ID collisions. Since IDs are spec-local L<N> values and findings record only limit, the brief and attestation cannot unambiguously identify which sealed limit was used; the gate accepts either one, so R3 attribution is ambiguous.

The ready-check treats the substring 'Accepted because' as a reason even when it ends the entry (for example, '- L1: assumption. Accepted because'). That unjustified limit is parsed and sealed, so R4's justification gate has a false pass.
ADR coverage uses substring matching for limit IDs. An ADR mentioning L10 therefore satisfies the required reference to L1, allowing an ADR that omits L1 to pass ready-check.
